newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN TRADERS SEE SHORT-TERM YIELDS EASE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN TRADERS SEE SHORT-TERM YIELDS EASE AGAIN.

text.p: Belgian T-bill and short-term rates will slip again once the Belgian national bank's policy of reducing liquidity to bolster the franc will have lifted the currency, traders said on Thursday.
Three-month T-bills, still at 3.22/27 percent on Thursday, were at 3.27/39 on Thursday. The one-week repo rate was at 3.35/40 percent against 3.24/28 a day earlier.
"No panic. The BNB has reduced liquidity to support the franc, the same tactics they always use," one trader said. "It has always been a successful policy so they'll stick to it," another said.
The franc was at 20.6420/30 to the mark, well above its ERM midpoint of 20.6255, but traders shrugged off the franc's relatively weak performance.
"It's not really so much that the franc is weak, but rather that the mark is strong," one said.
Another said he would only start worrying if the franc weakened weaken to 20.67. "But I don't believe this would happen...and even then...what's half a cent?" he said.
Traders said they were more worried about the French elections. Pressure on the French franc would automatically infect the Belgian franc, they said.

"People seem to be expecting an easy victory for the centre-right majority but the French never have had elections that went smoothly, the second round has often been a close affair," one trader said.
OLOs had a rough ride on the back of sagging Bund futures and weak Treasuries. Ten-year paper yielded 5.99 percent against 5.90 on Wednesday.
The spread, which had narrowed to five from nine basis points on Wednesday, was back at eight bp, exemplifying the fact that Belgium often lags a selloff Bund futures in a bear market.
